author: m. s. mccall
title: Pepperdine alumnus Mike Umbro discusses career in energy and sustainable power
text:
Mike Umbro, a 2005 graduate of Pepperdine University’s Seaver College, described his professional journey from student to founder and principal of FieldView Capital Advisors in an interview released on May 13. Umbro now leads the San Diego-based energy consultation firm, focusing on providing affordable and reliable energy solutions for California.
The discussion highlights how service-driven values learned at Pepperdine influenced Umbro’s approach to business and community engagement. His work centers on developing innovative techniques for sustainable power generation to support California’s residents and its power grid.
Reflecting on his time at Pepperdine, Umbro said, “Pepperdine was the strongest academic school that I was accepted to. All the stars aligned for me to enroll at Seaver College. My sister was in the midst of her degree there; I loved the community, the people; and as a native San Diegan, the campus’ proximity to the beach was a huge draw. To me, everything just seemed perfect about the opportunity. It was a great fit.” He also credited faculty mentors with helping him build a foundation for his future career: “I went in with an open mind, embraced the faculty mentors available to me, and built a strong foundation of knowledge to enter the workforce.”
Umbro described his introduction into energy through early roles sourcing oil and gas assets across the United States. He explained how learning about California’s high consumption rates motivated him: “The more I discovered about California’s energy dependencies, the more I wanted to figure out how I could help bring affordable, reliable energy to the state.”
Discussing current projects at FieldView Capital Advisors, he said they develop geological thermal energy storage projects known as GeoTES: “Essentially, GeoTES is a way to use a water reservoir as a reliable power source… we use concentrated solar mirrors to heat leftover fluids… At this hot temperature, we can dispatch hot water to a steam turbine power generator and create energy for California’s grid.” According to Umbro, this practice has been established in West Kern County and Central California through partnerships with national laboratories.
Looking ahead at his purpose beyond business success, Umbro said: “My greater purpose first and foremost is my family… Beyond that we’re called to love one another, and I try to live this out in my career by sharing my knowledge and investing my time in trying to make this state a better place for my neighbors.”
